relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis transmission occurs through a Lutzomyia sandfly bite, the primary dipteran vector genus propagating American cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, canine reservoir exposure, domestic dogs, zoonotic visceral leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis is maintained through canine reservoir exposure, where domestic dogs serve as the predominant vertebrate reservoir for zoonotic visceral leishmaniasis.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, sylvatic rodent habitat, wild reservoir, forest rodents, marsupials
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis involves environmental sylvatic rodent habitat exposure, where wild forest animals sustain endemic transmission cycles in Neotropical rainforests.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, cracked mud dwelling, earthen walls, rural housing, vector resting
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis risk is strongly linked to cracked mud dwelling residence, as microfissures in unplastered mud walls harbor breeding female sandflies.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, nocturnal outdoor sleeping, dusk to dawn exposure, night bites
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis risk rises drastically with nocturnal outdoor sleeping, exposing unprotected human skin to silent, dusk-to-dawn feeding phlebotomine sandflies.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, rainforest occupational exposure, chicle harvesters, loggers, soldiers
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis occurs following rainforest occupational exposure, directly introducing humans into undisturbed sylvatic sandfly and reservoir transmission niches.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Bihar endemic plains, Gangetic basin, anthroponotic kala-azar
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis is historically hyperendemic across the Bihar endemic plains, representing the world's most populous anthroponotic Leishmania donovani transmission corridor.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, East African savannah, Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis is heavily prevalent across the East African savannah, producing recurring epidemic outbreaks of visceral leishmaniasis with high case fatality.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Mediterranean basin travel, southern Europe, zoonotic infantum
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis is acquired through Mediterranean basin travel, frequently presenting as unexpected visceral disease in European tourists or immunocompromised individuals.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, Latin American rainforest, Amazon basin, Peru, Bolivia, Brazil
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis is heavily concentrated in Latin American rainforest regions, where diverse Leishmania species circulate among arboreal and terrestrial vectors.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, HIV AIDS coinfection, CD4 depletion, immunosuppression, visceral relapse
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis has a synergistic high-risk host relationship with HIV AIDS coinfection, triggering fulminant visceral symptoms, massive parasite loads, and frequent treatment relapses.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, protein energy malnutrition, zinc deficiency, impaired immunity
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis preferentially progresses in patients with protein energy malnutrition, converting asymptomatic Leishmania infection into lethal, overt clinical kala-azar.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pharmacologic immunosuppression, corticosteroids, organ transplant, anti-TNF
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis reactivates aggressively under pharmacologic immunosuppression, causing visceral reactivation in patients with previously quiescent latent Leishmania infections.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, intravenous needle sharing, bloodborne transmission, drug users
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis can be directly transmitted via intravenous needle sharing, bypassing insect vectors among urban drug abusers in Southern Europe.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, young pediatric age, infants, preschool children, zoonotic VL
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis exhibits peak susceptibility in young pediatric age groups, who comprise the vast majority of zoonotic Leishmania infantum cases in Latin America and the Mediterranean.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, nonimmune immigrant status, refugees, population displacement
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis triggers catastrophic epidemics among individuals with nonimmune immigrant status moving into hyperendemic transmission foci without acquired immunity.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, indolent incubation months, 2 to 8 months, delayed onset
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Leishmaniasis features an indolent incubation months timeframe for visceral disease, typically requiring 2 to 8 months between sandfly inoculation and full clinical illness.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, cutaneous incubation weeks, 2 to 8 weeks, bite papule
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Leishmaniasis features a cutaneous incubation weeks timeframe, wherein localized papules and ulcers emerge 2 to 8 weeks following the primary sandfly bite.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, delayed mucosal latency, espundia latency, years post-ulcer
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Leishmaniasis exhibits delayed mucosal latency, with destructive mucocutaneous espundia arising months to decades after the initial cutaneous sore has completely healed.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, termite mound proximity, sandfly resting, savannah microhabitat
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leishmaniasis exposure is heightened by termite mound proximity, which provides ideal cool, humid subterranean daytime resting sites for Phlebotomus sandflies.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, post conflict migration, war zones, disrupted vector control
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Leishmaniasis transmission explodes during post conflict migration, as documented during refugee displacements in Syria, Afghanistan, and South Sudan.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, marked leukocytosis, neutrophilia, pyogenic
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, which points strongly toward pyogenic bacterial sepsis or occult bacterial abscesses.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, absence of splenomegaly, normal spleen
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by absence of splenomegaly in prolonged febrile illness, as reticuloendothelial splenic parasitization invariably produces splenomegaly.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, anesthetic skin lesion, loss of sensation, leprosy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by an anesthetic skin lesion, as cutaneous leishmania lesions retain intact sensation, whereas tactile loss signifies tuberculoid leprosy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, painful purulent ulcer, acute pyoderma, bacterial
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by an acutely painful purulent ulcer, which indicates acute pyogenic bacterial pyoderma or ecthyma.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, enlarged peripheral nerves, nerve hypertrophy, leprosy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by enlarged peripheral nerves, a definitive neurological sign indicating Mycobacterium leprae neurotropism.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, acute onset 24 hours, hyperacute fever, dengue, malaria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by acute onset within 24 hours, as Leishmania requires weeks to months of indolent incubation before clinical manifestations emerge.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, overt jaundice, hyperbilirubinemia, viral hepatitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by hyperbilirubinemic overt jaundice at admission, which signifies acute viral hepatitis, biliary sepsis, or Weil disease.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, intrahepatic cystic lesions, liver cysts, hydatid
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Leishmaniasis is ruled out by intrahepatic cystic lesions on ultrasound, an imaging finding pathognomonic of cystic echinococcosis or amebic abscess.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, rapid antibacterial response, beta lactam defervescence
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Leishmaniasis is ruled out by rapid antibacterial response to standard beta-lactams, as Leishmania protozoa are completely refractory to antibacterial antibiotics.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, absolute eosinophilia, eosinophils > 3000, helminth
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by marked absolute eosinophilia, as leishmaniasis typically causes eosinopenia or neutropenia, whereas extreme eosinophilia indicates invasive helminthiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, circulating peripheral blasts, myeloblasts, leukemia
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by circulating peripheral blasts on admission blood smear, which establishes a primary hematological malignancy such as acute leukemia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, intraerythrocytic plasmodial rings, malaria trophozoites
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Leishmaniasis as the primary etiology of acute fever is ruled out by intraerythrocytic plasmodial rings on blood film, confirming active malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, pipestem periportal fibrosis, Symmers fibrosis, schistosoma
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by pipestem periportal fibrosis on ultrasound, a pathognomonic hallmark of chronic hepatosplenic schistosomiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, acid fast bacilli, positive Ziehl Neelsen, mycobacteria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by abundant acid fast bacilli on lesion smear, confirming cutaneous tuberculosis, leprosy, or Buruli ulcer.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, centrally painful eschar, tender black necrosis, rickettsia
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by a centrally painful eschar with acute regional toxemia, which indicates scrub typhus or cutaneous anthrax.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, caseating necrosis, caseous granuloma, tuberculosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by extensive caseating granulomatous necrosis on biopsy, which points decisively toward mycobacterial tuberculosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, normal serum immunoglobulins, normal IgG, normal protein
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Chronic visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by normal serum immunoglobulins, as prolonged visceral disease invariably triggers massive polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, prompt antimalarial response, artemisinin cure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by prompt antimalarial response within 48 hours of artemisinin administration, as antimalarials exert no antileishmanial activity.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, pure scalp lesions, hairy scalp, sparing
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is ruled out by lesions confined purely to the scalp, as sandflies rarely penetrate thick scalp hair to bite, sparing this anatomical site.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, solitary lung cavitation, apical cavity, tuberculosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Primary visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by solitary lung cavitation on chest radiography, which establishes active cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, normal spleen size, no splenomegaly, ultrasound normal
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by strictly normal spleen size on ultrasound, as reticuloendothelial proliferation inevitably produces sonographically detectable splenomegaly.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, severe hemolysis bilirubin, dark urine, hemoglobinuria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Visceral leishmaniasis is ruled out by acute severe hemolysis with hemoglobinuria, which indicates blackwater fever, severe G6PD crisis, or autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, malaria, Plasmodium, blood film, intraerythrocytic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from malaria by double-peaking daily fevers, profound leukopenia, astronomical hypergammaglobulinemia, and presence of LD bodies on marrow aspirate rather than intraerythrocytic plasmodia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, schistosomiasis, Symmers fibrosis, portal hypertension
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from schistosomiasis by prolonged high fevers, profound pancytopenia, and marrow amastigotes, whereas hepatosplenic schistosomiasis is afebrile with periportal pipestem fibrosis on ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, leprosy, Mycobacterium leprae, anesthetic patch, thickened nerves
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from leprosy by completely preserved cutaneous sensation within ulcers, lack of peripheral nerve thickening, and intracellular amastigotes rather than acid-fast globi.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, cutaneous anthrax, Bacillus anthracis, black eschar, gelatinous edema
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from cutaneous anthrax by chronic indolent duration over weeks to months with granular crater bases, whereas anthrax causes rapid 48-hour black eschar with striking gelatinous non-pitting edema.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, disseminated histoplasmosis, Histoplasma capsulatum, intracellular yeast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from disseminated histoplasmosis by identification of a rod-shaped purplish kinetoplast in amastigotes, whereas Histoplasma yeasts exhibit narrow-based budding without kinetoplast structures.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, visceral brucellosis, Brucella melitensis, undulant fever, unpasteurized milk
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from visceral brucellosis by massive splenomegaly reaching the pelvic brim, extreme hypergammaglobulinemia, positive rK39 dipstick, and lack of response to doxycycline-rifampin regimens.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, typhoid fever, enteric fever, Salmonella Typhi, stepladder fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from typhoid fever by subacute indolent progression over months rather than an acute 1-to-2 week stepladder fever, absence of relative bradycardia, and refractoriness to ceftriaxone.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly, HMS, high IgM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from tropical splenomegaly syndrome (HMS) by persistent fevers, extreme polyclonal IgG elevation rather than selective IgM spikes, and demonstration of LD amastigotes on bone marrow.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, cutaneous tuberculosis, lupus vulgaris, scrofuloderma, apple jelly
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from cutaneous tuberculosis (lupus vulgaris) by absence of yellowish apple-jelly nodules on diascopy, absence of caseous necrosis on biopsy, and demonstration of intracellular amastigotes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, acute myeloid leukemia, AML, blast cells, marrow infiltration
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from acute myeloid leukemia by absence of clonal myeloblasts on marrow aspirate and identification of diagnostic Leishman-Donovan amastigotes within normal histiocytic elements.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, Hodgkin lymphoma, Pel Ebstein fever, Reed Sternberg cells
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from Hodgkin lymphoma by prominent pancytopenia, massive diffuse splenic enlargement, and absence of characteristic binucleate Reed-Sternberg giant cells on nodal biopsy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, amebic liver abscess, Entamoeba histolytica, anchovy sauce, cystic cavity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from amebic liver abscess by marked splenomegaly, profound leukopenia, and homogeneous hepatic ultrasound, whereas amebic abscess shows focal liquefactive cavities with anchovy-paste aspirate.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, bacterial pyoderma, ecthyma, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from bacterial pyoderma (ecthyma) by its indolent weeks-to-months course, painless crater with rolled violaceous border, and complete lack of response to first-generation cephalosporins.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, sporotrichosis, Sporothrix schenckii, rose gardener, nodular lymphangitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from sporotrichosis by identification of kinetoplast-containing amastigotes on smear, lack of fungal cigar-shaped budding yeasts on PAS stain, and sandfly rather than thorn exposure.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, yaws, Treponema pallidum pertenue, frambesia, papilloma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from yaws by negative rapid treponemal serology, absence of spirochetes on darkfield microscopy, and complete refractoriness to single-dose intramuscular benzathine penicillin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, paracoccidioidomycosis, Paracoccidioides, mariner's wheel, mulberry stomatitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from paracoccidioidomycosis by absence of pathognomonic mariner's wheel multi-budding yeasts on direct KOH examination and presence of LD amastigotes inside mucosal histiocytes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, chromoblastomycosis, muriform cells, Medlar bodies, verrucous plaque
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from chromoblastomycosis by absence of pigmented thick-walled sclerotic muriform Medlar bodies ('copper pennies') on 10% KOH scrapings of skin lesions.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, Buruli ulcer, Mycobacterium ulcerans, undermined borders, mycolactone necrosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from Buruli ulcer by rolled raised violaceous indurated borders rather than widely undermined necrotic edges, and demonstration of amastigotes rather than acid-fast bacilli in subcutaneous fat.
